reason: Every opcode is standard 65C02 that the 65SC12 has (STZ zp, ORA #, CPY #, LDY zp, EOR zp; no Rockwell bit ops). Recount, crossing path from the old STA unused_0076 to RTS: old 68 cycles with both BCS taken (69/70 when one or both wraps happen), 52 bytes; new 54 cycles straight-line, 37 bytes. That saves 14 to 16 cycles and 15 bytes, matching the claim of 14.2. ru_lo, ru_d and unused_0076 move from absolute to zero page in two places (-1 cycle each). The ru_cells_lo/hi,Y reads stay in one page: ship/bench &0A80-&0A8F after the 15-byte shift, gameplay &09CE-&09DD. ground_columns and um_next stay inside their pages in both layouts, so their ASSERTs hold. The inside-cell path's BRA ru_done only gets shorter and stays in the same page, and no hot code follows the section. Self-modifying code: none touches this region. vertical_rows_jsr_b245f+1 patches only the caller's JSR low byte, and ru_lo/ru_d/unused_0076 are read only inside rows_up and add_Y_rows. bank5's unused_0076+1 is &77, and neither the IRQ nor the renderer reads &76. On the crossing path ru_lo is no longer written, but it is read nowhere after this point, and every call re-stores it at entry, so a Y>=8 read of ru_cells_hi+8 (=ru_lo) would still see the same byte. The single ORA #&40 wrap equals the two CMP/ADC wraps whenever X is &40-&7F and Y<=7: v1 is &2E-&7F and t is &2B-&7F, checked case by case. The arithmetic fails for X>=&80 or X=&00-&02 edge cases (for example X=0 with an initial zero mover address). So I probed the base ship build, the whole world from a cold first game with the WorldBot: 11,412 passes to completion, 28,285 rows_up calls, 26,399 on the crossing path. Every X was in &40-&7F, the largest Y was 4, and none were out of range. C and V on exit change. Callers: plot_mover_sprite/walk_column CLC before using C; move_mover_right/left CLC/SEC; the projectile path through add_Y_rows reaches CPX #&05 before any flag read. No BVC/BVS follows. A, X, Y and unused_0076=0 on exit are unchanged.
